metadata.title: AI Sovereignty Lab Scenario Catalogue
metadata.purpose: Define transparent browser-executable dependency scenarios without predicting geopolitical events.

scenarios.label: Loss of access to frontier accelerators
questions: Which model labs can continue inference on existing installed capacity?
Which ecosystems can train or fine-tune without new imported accelerators?
Which domestic or allied substitutes exist, and at what performance level?
How long can installed hardware operate without replacement parts and software support?

initial_impact_rules.condition: ecosystem has installed local capacity but no domestic supply path
replacement and installed-base data are missing

scenarios.label: High-bandwidth memory supply disruption
questions: Which accelerator deployments depend on the affected memory generation?
Can alternative memory suppliers qualify in time?
Does local accelerator ownership matter when memory supply is external?

initial_impact_rules.condition: edge from HBM supplier to accelerator layer has low substitutability
no qualified alternate supply is represented

scenarios.label: Restriction on leading-edge lithography equipment
questions: Which fabs can continue current production but cannot expand or advance process nodes?
Which equipment, service and spare-part dependencies remain even when machines are already installed?
How long before the restriction affects accelerator availability?

initial_impact_rules.condition: fabrication node depends on EUV and has no substitute equipment path
scenario duration exceeds maintenance or expansion tolerance

scenarios.label: Loss of access to a foreign hyperscaler control plane
questions: Can locally hosted workloads continue without the foreign control plane?
Who controls identities, encryption keys, billing and service activation?
Can workloads move to another local provider or self-hosted infrastructure?
Which managed services have no portable replacement?

initial_impact_rules.condition: capability status is foreign_owned_locally_hosted and no alternate provider exists
portable workload and tested alternate provider exist
managed proprietary service is essential and nonportable

scenarios.label: Data-center power and grid constraint
questions: Which facilities lose power or cannot expand?
Which workloads can be prioritized or shifted?
Is backup generation sufficient for continuous AI operation?
Does the ecosystem control fuel, generation, grid connection and cooling?

initial_impact_rules.condition: data-center node has a single critical power dependency
planned compute cannot obtain grid connection
multi-site capacity and tested workload shifting exist

scenarios.label: International submarine connectivity disruption
questions: Which cloud, API and data-transfer paths depend on the affected routes?
Which alternate landing points and terrestrial routes are available?
Can domestic services continue in an isolated national mode?
How much model and application functionality requires real-time foreign access?

initial_impact_rules.condition: critical service requires a foreign API and all relevant routes fail
route and capacity data are missing

implementation_rule: Every scenario result must display the dependency path and the evidence or assumption used. No scenario may be described as a forecast.
